title: How messy is 2 4 1 3 5?
hook: Count the pairs that are out of order. Is checking every pair the only way?

knows: merging two sorted lists by taking the smaller front card (merge-sort-payoff)
doesNotKnow: that one pass of merging also counts how far a list is from sorted
that counting out-of-order pairs can cost far fewer than n(n-1)/2 checks

misconception: Counting out-of-order pairs means checking every pair, which is n(n-1)/2 checks.
objective: The learner can merge [2 4] and [1 3 5], add the number of left cards still waiting each time a right card is taken, reach 3 out-of-order pairs, and explain why this counting is free during merge sort (O(n log n) total).

claims.source: Builder's node check (2026-10-14): brute force over all 10 pairs gives exactly (2,1), (4,1), (4,3); control lists: 5 4 3 2 1 gives 10, 1 2 3 4 5 gives 0. Demo.tsx BRUTE recomputes the list for the reveal. Unverified. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): verified. Brute force over all 10 pairs of 2 4 1 3 5 gives (2,1), (4,1), (4,3); Demo.tsx BRUTE uses the same rule.

claims.text: Each half, [2 4] and [1 3 5], is already in order, so no out-of-order pair sits inside a half.
claims.source: 2 < 4 and 1 < 3 < 5 by inspection. Unverified. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): verified. 2 < 4 and 1 < 3 < 5; stage says 'Each half is already in order'.

claims.text: When a right-half card is taken, it is smaller than every left card still waiting, so it forms one out-of-order pair with each: 1 jumps 2 and 4 (+2), 3 jumps 4 (+1), 5 jumps nobody.
claims.source: The left half is sorted and the merge takes the smaller front card, so a right card taken first is smaller than the left front and hence every waiting left card; each such left card came earlier in the list. Builder's node merge log: 1(+2), 2, 3(+1), 4, 5(+0). Demo.tsx STEPS recomputes it. Unverified. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): verified. Re-ran Demo.tsx STEPS merge (take left on <=): 1(+2), 2, 3(+1), 4, 5(+0). A right card is taken only when strictly smaller than the left front, so it is smaller than every waiting left card.

claims.text: Counting during the merge gives the same answer as checking every pair.
claims.source: Builder's node check (2026-10-14): merge-sort count equals brute-force count on all 720 orders of 1..6 (brief cs.algorithms.md #54 claim 2). Unverified. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): verified. Independent merge-sort counter vs brute force on all 720 orders of 1..6: 0 mismatches.

claims.text: Checking every pair of 5 cards takes 10 checks and finds the same 3; the merge found them in 5 takes.
claims.source: 5 x 4 / 2 = 10 pairs; the merge takes one card per step, 5 cards. Unverified. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): verified. 5*4/2 = 10 (Demo.tsx ALL_PAIRS); STEPS.length = 5. | REWORDED v2 (builder, 2026-10-14): Now shown on stage: 'Check every pair' sets the readout 'Every pair: checks 10, 3 found' beside 'Merge: takes 5 of 5'. Reveal quotes the takes from the learner's recorded full merge. Unverified. | FC pass 24 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. 5 x 4 / 2 = 10 = ALL_PAIRS; BRUTE has 3 pairs; STEPS.length = 5. Readout 'Every pair: checks 10, 3 found' after the brute milestone. rec.takes is always 5 because a record is written only when a merge finishes.

claims.text: Merge sort repeats this merge at every level, so counting this way costs O(n log n) in total, not n².
claims.source: CLRS 4th ed. chapter 2, problem 2-4 (inversions: count in Theta(n lg n) worst case by modifying merge sort); 3rd ed. problem 2-4. Unverified. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): verified. Derivation stands alone: merge sort is O(n log n) and counting adds O(1) per card taken. CLRS problem 2-4 (Inversions, 'modify merge sort', Theta(n lg n)) cited from memory, book not opened; the learner sentence does not depend on it. | REWORDED v2 (builder, 2026-10-14): Wording only ('splits and merges' -> 'repeats this merge'). Context sentence, told; the derivation in the pass-21 note stands (merge sort O(n log n) plus O(1) per card taken). Unverified. | FC pass 24 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Derivation (CLRS problem 2-4 not opened): merge sort has log n levels of O(n) merging, and each take adds the waiting-left count (O(1)), so the total is O(n log n). Wording change only.

claims.text: Hook: checking every pair is one way to count out-of-order pairs, but not the only way.
claims.source: Builder (2026-10-14, v2): the stage shows both: 'Check every pair' (10 checks) and the merge count (5 takes) give the same 3; c4 covers that the two methods agree in general. Unverified. | FC pass 24 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Hook 'Is checking every pair the only way?'; the stage counts the same 3 two ways (10 pair checks, merge in 5 takes), and c4 (pass 21) covers agreement on all orders.

recall.question: During a merge, a card from the right half is taken while 3 cards still wait in the left half. How many out-of-order pairs does that one step reveal?
recall.why: The taken card is smaller than every left card still waiting, and each of them came earlier, so it makes one out-of-order pair with each of the 3.
